app_exercised: Exercised FuelWell web app across 6+ routes at http://localhost:3000 using Playwright automation targeting personas P77 (program director, 50, projector presenter), P78 (recovering perfectionist tracker, 26), P79 (left-handed carpenter, 39, 6.7" phone), and P80 (localization-minded expat, 34, metric/imperial). Visited /preview (demo hub), /app/dashboard (macros), /app/log (meal search & entry), /app/nutrition (detail), /app/meal-plan (empty state), /app/progress (trends), /app/settings (preferences), /app/recipes, /app/grocery-list. Tested at viewports 375px, 390px (mobile), and 1024px (projector). Performed interactions: keyboard Tab navigation, form submission attempts, mouse hover, long text input, empty state inspection. Captured 17 evidence screenshots (A20-*.png). Ran assertions on font sizes, touch target dimensions (44px minimum), button positioning for left-thumb reach (0-200px from left edge), color contrast ratios, unit consistency, date formatting, message tone (shame language scan), keyboard focus visibility, and form validation feedback.

findings.description: "Over target" messaging uses shame language instead of neutral reporting
reproduction_steps: Log meals that exceed calorie or macro targets
findings.observed_evidence: Dashboard text frames macros using judgment language: "350 kcal over target" implies failure rather than data. For P78 (recovering perfectionist tracker), this language triggers relapse anxiety about perfectionism. Screenshot A20-p78-dashboard-tone.png shows the exact wording.
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe all over-target text to neutral data: "350 kcal above target" (fact) not "you exceeded" (judgment). Avoid "over", "exceeded", "should have". This is critical for P78's mental health and sustained app use.

findings.description: Small font sizes (<14px) difficult to read on projected display
reproduction_steps: Visit /preview demo hub (where P77 presents to committees)
findings.observed_evidence: Preview hub contains multiple <14px text: 'New in v1.4.0: Daily nutrition + fitness' (P tag, 12px), 'Retry' button (12px). At projector viewing distance (15+ feet), 12px appears blurry. Screenshot A20-p77-preview-detail.png.
findings.suggested_fix: Enforce ≥14px minimum body text, 20px+ for headings on /preview. Test actual layout on conference room projector before demo day.

findings.description: Empty meal plan state messaging tone is dismissive or obligatory
reproduction_steps: Visit /app/meal-plan with fresh account (no meals planned)
Read empty state heading and body text
findings.observed_evidence: Empty state text: 'Your next step is to fill the open dinner and lunch...' frames planning as obligation. P78 reads 'next step' and 'fill' as 'must complete', triggering perfectionist anxiety. Screenshot A20-p78-mealplan-empty.png.
findings.suggested_fix: Use invitational tone: 'Ready to plan ahead? Start whenever you'd like.' Avoid 'must', 'need to', 'required', 'complete', 'next step' (imperatives).

findings.description: /app/log: Key actions positioned at right edge, unreachable for left-thumb user
reproduction_steps: Measure button center positions from left edge
findings.observed_evidence: Critical action buttons positioned at x=318px and x=358px from left (unreachable for left-thumb on 390px width). Carpenter with gloved hands cannot reach right edge without hand shift. Screenshot A20-p79-button-spacing.png.
findings.suggested_fix: Center actions within 0-200px horizontal range. Ensure all touch targets ≥44x44px. Test one-handed left-thumb interaction on actual 6.7" phone.

findings.description: Text is truncated or overflows at 375px width, unreadable without expanding
reproduction_steps: Observe macro summary and meal descriptions
findings.observed_evidence: Found 4 text elements clipped or with width=0: 'Daily decision system' (0px), 'Log dinner to keep it alive to' (truncated). User must tap/expand to read. Screenshot A20-p79-mobile-375.png.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply Tailwind line-clamp-2 for known-long text; use ellipsis. Test layout at 320px minimum width.

findings.description: Icon-only buttons have no text, aria-label, or title for screen readers
reproduction_steps: Inspect buttons with only SVG icons (close, menu, settings, search, notifications)
Check HTML for aria-label and title attributes
findings.observed_evidence: Found 6 icon-only buttons lacking aria-label or title. Screen reader user hears generic 'button' with no context. Screenshot inspection shows empty button text nodes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add aria-label to every icon-only button: `<button aria-label="Close menu">×</button>`. As fallback, add title attribute.

findings.description: Inconsistent number formatting: some use commas (1,400) some don't (1400)
reproduction_steps: Scan all calorie and macro numbers for comma usage
findings.observed_evidence: Mix of comma-formatted ('2,250 kcal') and non-comma ('850 kcal') on same view. Metric-preference user expects consistent formatting per locale (en-GB uses thousands separator consistently).
findings.suggested_fix: Use Intl.NumberFormat(userLocale) for all numbers. Choose one format globally and enforce via design tokens.

findings.description: Dashboard macro cards use inconsistent spacing, unclear visual hierarchy between targets and actuals
reproduction_steps: Compare visual separation between target and actual values
findings.observed_evidence: Macro cards show target/actual stacked without clear visual distinction. P78 experiences 'is this the target or actual?' second-guessing (perfectionist pattern). Screenshot A20-p78-spacing-hierarchy.png.
findings.suggested_fix: Use consistent spacing: 4px gaps for sub-items, 16px for sections. Label target (lighter) and actual (emphasis) distinctly by color/weight.

findings.description: /preview hub navigation links lack clear affordance, hard to distinguish from body text
reproduction_steps: Look at section headings ('1. Existing user preview', '2. New user signup')
Try to identify clickable vs. descriptive text
findings.observed_evidence: Preview sections are labeled but lack CTA styling (button look, hover change, icon). Program director presenting to committee cannot quickly identify next clickable item. Screenshot A20-p77-preview-labels.png.
findings.suggested_fix: Make section headings explicit CTAs: add button styling (background, padding), icon (→), or ensure clear color/underline on hover.

findings.description: CTA buttons <40px height are small click targets on projector
findings.observed_evidence: 'Retry' button measured at 34px tall. Small height makes clicking difficult with projector-room mouse from distance (10+ feet). Screenshot A20-p77-preview-detail.png.
findings.suggested_fix: Set minimum ≥40px button heights for /preview paths. Increase padding (Tailwind py-3). Test clickability at arm's length.

findings.description: Mobile (390px): Text-background color contrast may be insufficient
reproduction_steps: Use DevTools to inspect computed color values
findings.observed_evidence: Found 5 text elements below WCAG AA threshold (≥4.5:1 for body text, ≥3:1 for UI). Carpenter with presbyopia or in low-light job-site breaks cannot read low-contrast text.
findings.suggested_fix: Run Axe DevTools or WebAIM contrast checker on all text. Ensure ≥4.5:1 contrast. Use Tailwind color tokens ensuring dark on light or light on dark.

findings.description: Projector (1024px): Text-background color contrast may be insufficient
findings.observed_evidence: 5 elements below AA threshold at projector resolution. Projector reduces perceived contrast (lower brightness, large viewing angle). Program director cannot rely on readability at projector brightness.
findings.suggested_fix: Target AAA contrast (7:1 for text) on /preview. Use high-saturation, high-luminance color pairs. Test on actual projector screen.

findings.observed_evidence: Dashboard uses three terms: '1400 calories' (full), '2250 kcal' (abbrev), '850 cal' (short). Metric-accent user (en-GB) familiar with SI units expects consistent 'kcal' throughout.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize on 'kcal' everywhere (scientifically correct, unambiguous). Never use 'calories' alone or 'cal' (too brief).

findings.description: Log page action buttons ("Snap Photo", "Ask Coach", "Scan Barcode") are too closely spaced, cause accidental mis-taps
reproduction_steps: Look at 4 quick-action buttons below search
findings.observed_evidence: Action buttons aligned horizontally with minimal gap between touch targets. Carpenter with coarse hands or glove residue easily mis-taps adjacent button. Screenshot A20-p79-button-spacing.png.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 12px gap between buttons (Tailwind gap-3). Increase padding to 44x44px minimum per button. Test with gloved hand.

findings.description: Log form has excessive instructional language ("Please enter", "Click here", "Type your search")
reproduction_steps: Read all labels, placeholders, helper text
findings.observed_evidence: Form text: 'Please search for a food', 'Type in your search', 'Click to add'. Found 7 instructional word instances. P78 (already anxious, cognitively loaded) feels talked-down to.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove 'please' (sounds supplicating). Use placeholder text instead of labels ('Banana, yogurt, ...' not 'Search for food name'). Button: 'Log Meal' is clear without 'Click here to log meal'.

findings.description: Search input overflows with very long text, becomes hard to edit
reproduction_steps: Attempt to edit beginning of text
findings.observed_evidence: Input accepts very long strings. scrollWidth=934px exceeds box width=308px. User cannot see or edit start of long names (e.g., 'Organic cold-pressed extra-virgin coconut oil...'). QA contractor testing edge cases identifies this.
findings.suggested_fix: Truncate input at 60 characters (reasonable max food name length), or ensure horizontal scroll with clear affordance indicator.

findings.description: Unit preference toggle (Metric/Imperial) in Settings does not persist to other pages. Weight and height fields remain hardcoded to imperial (LB, IN) regardless of user selection.
reproduction_steps: Navigate to http://localhost:3000/app/settings on mobile (en-GB locale)
Observe WEIGHT IN POUNDS and HEIGHT IN INCHES labels
Click the Metric button to switch units
Verify that labels change to WEIGHT IN KILOGRAMS and HEIGHT IN CENTIMETERS
Check the TODAY'S WEIGHT field and Start/Goal weight display
findings.observed_evidence: After clicking Metric button in Settings, the page still displays 'WEIGHT IN POUNDS' and 'HEIGHT IN INCHES'. No unit conversion occurs. On /app/progress, weight is shown as '186.4 lb' and 'Goal 178.0 lb' with only 'LB' label, no KG option. Metric button shows aria-pressed=true but units remain imperial throughout the app.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement unit preference persistence. Store the Imperial/Metric toggle state in user settings or localStorage, then use it to conditionally render unit labels (kg/lbs) and convert stored weight values on pages like /app/progress. Ensure the weight input field in the progress mock entry respects the user's unit preference.

findings.description: Meal plan date format uses US month abbreviation order (Mon, Jun 8) instead of locale-native en-GB format (Mon, 8 Jun). While unambiguous, it is not culturally localized for users with en-GB browser locale.
reproduction_steps: Set browser locale to en-GB and timezone to Europe/London
Observe the date labels on day cards (Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu labels)
Compare to expected en-GB date format standards
findings.observed_evidence: Meal plan displays dates as 'Mon, Jun 8', 'Tue, Jun 9', 'Wed, Jun 10', 'Thu, Jun 11' using month-first abbreviation. For en-GB locale, the native format would be 'Mon, 8 Jun' (date before month) or 'Monday 8 June'. The current format is US-centric and ignores the browser's locale settings.
findings.suggested_fix: Use browser locale to format dates. Import date-fns, luxon, or Intl.DateTimeFormat to format meal plan dates according to the user's locale. For en-GB, output 'Mon, 8 Jun' or 'Monday 8 June'. Ensure date formatting is consistent across all pages (/app/meal-plan, /app/daily-review, /app/progress).
